source_text:
Ἡμεῖς δὲ λέγομεν αὐτὸν
εἶναι ἄνθρωπον ὁμοιοπαθῆ ἡμῖν καὶ μήτε μείζονα Χριστοῦ, ἀλλ' οὔτε Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ, οὔτε μὴν εἶναι αὐτὸν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον. Ὅτι δὲ οὐκ ἔστι μείζων τοῦ Χριστοῦ, εἰπάτωσαν ἡμῖν οἱ τοῦτο λέγοντες ποίου χωρίου αὐτὸν εἶναι λέγουσιν; ἆρα οὐρανίου; ἆρα ἐπιγείου ἢ καταχθονίου; Εἰ μὲν οὐρανίου ἢ ἄλλου τινὸς χωρίου, ἀκουσάτωσαν ὅτι αὐτῷ κάμψει πᾶν γόνυ καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Εἰ οὖν κάμπτει γόνυ, ἐλάττων εἴη ὁ προσκυνῶν τοῦ προσκυνουμένου Χριστοῦ. Ἀλλ' οὔτε τὸν ἐπιόντα στίχον ἴσασιν οἱ τάλανες· τῷ ἀφομοιουμένῳ τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ· ὥσπερ καὶ ἡμεῖς κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ ὁμοίωσιν Θεοῦ ἐγενόμεθα. Ἀλλ' ἴσως τις ἐπερωτᾷ τῶν ἀκροατῶν καὶ λέγει· τί οὖν ἔστι τὸ ἀπάτορα αὐτὸν λέγεσθαι καὶ ἀμήτορα καὶ ἀγενεαλόγητον; Πρὸς ὃν ἐροῦμεν ὅτι Ἰουδαῖοι μὲν αὐτὸν εἰρήκασιν ἐκ πόρνης γεννηθῆναι καὶ διὰ τοῦτο μὴ γενεαλογηθῆναι ὑπὸ τῆς γραφῆς. Πρὸς οὓς ἐροῦμεν ὅτι κακῶς εἴπατε. Εὑρίσκομεν γὰρ καὶ ἄλλους ἐκ πόρνης γεννηθέντας καὶ γενεαλογηθέντας· εὐθὺς ὁ Σολομῶν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου, εἶτα καὶ ὁ Ἀβιμέλεχ υἱὸς Γεδεών. Τίνος οὖν ἕνεκεν οὐ γενεαλογεῖται; Ἐπειδὴ τύπος ἦν τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τούτου εἰκόνα ἔφερε, διὰ τοῦτο παρέλιπεν αὐτοῦ ἡ γραφὴ τὸν πατέρα καὶ μητέρα, ἵνα ἐν ἐκείνῳ καθάπερ εἰκόνι τὸν ἀληθῶς ἀπάτορα καὶ ἀμήτορα καὶ ἀγενεαλόγητον Χριστὸν ἐνοπτρισώμεθα.
thought_title: Melchizedek is human, not greater than Christ, and his missing genealogy is a type
orientation: Chrysostom is reporting the orthodox reply to those who said Melchizedek was greater than Christ or was the Holy Spirit, and to Jews who said he was born of a prostitute.
pass_a_gloss: But we say that he is a human being with feelings like ours and neither greater than Christ, but not even than John the Baptist, nor indeed that he is the Holy Spirit. And that he is not greater than Christ, let those who say this tell us: of what region do they say he is? Is it heavenly? Is it earthly or subterranean? If heavenly or of some other region, let them hear that to him every knee will bend and so on. If therefore he bends the knee, the one who worships would be less than the Christ who is worshipped. But the wretched ones do not even know the coming verse: to the one being made like the Son of God; just as we also came into being according to the image and likeness of God. But perhaps one of the hearers asks and says: what then is it that he is called without father and without mother and without genealogy? To whom we will say that the Jews have said that he was born from a prostitute and for this reason was not genealogized by the Scripture. To whom we will say: you have spoken badly. For we find also others born from a prostitute and genealogized: immediately Solomon from the wife of Uriah, then also Abimelech son of Gideon. For what reason then is he not genealogized? Because he was a type of Christ and bore his image, for this reason the Scripture omitted his father and mother, so that in him as in an image we might behold as in a mirror the truly without father and without mother and without genealogy Christ.

lemmas.gloss: to behold as in a mirror
to the one being made like

choices.why: Glossary term; keeps the sense of shared human passibility without the banned 'of like nature'.

choices.english: without father... without mother... without genealogy
choices.why: Glossary terms; the triple formula from Hebrews 7:3 must stay consistent.

choices.english: he was a type of Christ
choices.why: Glossary term; 'type' is the fixed rendering for τύπος.
Glossary term; 'image' is the fixed rendering for εἰκών.

choices.english: we might behold as in a mirror
choices.why: The verb is from ἔνοπτρον (mirror); the rendering preserves the mirror metaphor that the Greek carries.
Keeps the passive force of the Greek and the glossary verb γενεαλογέω.

pass_b_english: But we say that he was a human being with feelings like ours, not greater than Christ—nor even greater than John the Baptist—and certainly not the Holy Spirit. As for the claim that he is greater than Christ, let those who say this tell us: what region do they say he belongs to? Is it heavenly? Is it earthly or under the earth? If it is heavenly or some other region, let them hear that to him every knee will bend, and so on (Philippians 2:10). If every knee bends, then the one who worships would be less than the Christ who is worshipped. But the wretched people do not even know the next line: “being made like the Son of God”—just as we also came into being according to the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:26).

But perhaps one of the hearers asks and says: What then does it mean that he is called without father, without mother, and without genealogy? To him we will answer that the Jews have said he was born of a prostitute, and for that reason Scripture did not trace his genealogy. To them we will answer: You have spoken wrongly. For we find others who were born of a prostitute and yet had their genealogy traced—immediately Solomon, born of Uriah’s wife, and then Abimelech, the son of Gideon. Why then is his genealogy not traced? Because he was a type of Christ and bore his image. For this reason Scripture omitted his father and mother, so that in him, as in an image, we might behold as in a mirror the Christ who is truly without father, without mother, and without genealogy.

last_rejected.quote: But perhaps one of the hearers asks and says
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλ' ἴσως τις ἐπερωτᾷ τῶν ἀκροατῶν καὶ λέγει
last_rejected.why: The English marks this as the interlocutor's speech, but the source has the interlocutor asking a question, and the author ('we') answering. The English correctly attributes 'But perhaps one of the hearers asks' to the interlocutor. However, 'To him we will answer' and 'To them we will answer' correctly show the author responding. This seems correct.
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly attributes question to hearer; author answers. No error.

last_rejected.why: The Greek has ἐλάττων εἴη (optative with ἄν implied by conditional εἰ), 'would be less'. The English 'would be less' correctly renders the potential optative in a conditional. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐλάττων εἴη (optative) correctly rendered 'would be less'.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'trace a genealogy' for γενεαλογέω. The English uses 'trace his genealogy' which is the passive form with object 'his'. This is within normal range. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: 'trace his genealogy' is within normal range for γενεαλογέω.

last_rejected.quote: not greater than Christ—nor even greater than John the Baptist
last_rejected.source_quote: μήτε μείζονα Χριστοῦ, ἀλλ' οὔτε Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ
last_rejected.why: The Greek says 'neither greater than Christ, but not even than John the Baptist'. The English 'not greater than Christ—nor even greater than John the Baptist' captures this well. The ἀλλ' οὔτε = 'but not even'. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀλλ' οὔτε correctly rendered 'nor even'. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.source_quote: οὔτε μὴν εἶναι αὐτὸν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον
last_rejected.why: οὔτε μὴν = 'and certainly not' or 'nor indeed'. The English 'certainly not' captures the emphasis. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: οὔτε μὴν correctly rendered 'certainly not'. Emphasis captured.

last_rejected.quote: To him we will answer that the Jews have said
last_rejected.source_quote: Πρὸς ὃν ἐροῦμεν ὅτι Ἰουδαῖοι μὲν αὐτὸν εἰρήκασιν
last_rejected.why: The source marks 'the Jews have said' as a report of their claim. The English correctly attributes this to 'the Jews' as a reported speaker. The 'we will answer' shows the author speaking. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Πρὸς ὃν ἐροῦμεν correctly rendered; Jews as reported speakers.

last_rejected.quote: To them we will answer: You have spoken wrongly
last_rejected.source_quote: Πρὸς οὓς ἐροῦμεν ὅτι κακῶς εἴπατε
last_rejected.why: The English uses 'To them we will answer' addressing the Jews, with direct quote 'You have spoken wrongly'. This correctly represents the author's response to the Jews' claim. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Πρὸς οὓς ἐροῦμεν correctly addresses Jews; direct quote preserved.

last_rejected.why: Present passive indicative 'is not genealogized'. The English 'is his genealogy not traced' uses present passive sense. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: οὐ γενεαλογεῖται present passive correctly rendered 'is not traced'.

problems.why: The phrase shifts between 'without mother and without father,' 'without father and without mother,' and the expanded 'without father, without mother, and without genealogy,' with the final section adding 'on earth'/'in heaven' qualifiers that radically reframe the meaning. A reader may not track that these are the same formula being reinterpreted.
problems.fix: Keep consistent order or flag the exegetical expansion.

variants.text: without father, without mother, and without genealogy
without father on earth according to the flesh, and without mother in the heavens according to the spirit
without father, without mother, and without genealogy

problems.quote: But perhaps one of the hearers asks and says
problems.why: Shifts to imagined interlocutor without clear marking; the 'we' that answers is also unclear after the 'Chrysostom' insertion.
problems.fix: Format as dialogue or add attribution.

problems.quote: To them we will answer: You have spoken wrongly
problems.why: The 'them' refers to 'the Jews' mentioned two sentences back, but 'we will answer' creates confusion about who speaks and to whom.
problems.fix: Clarify 'the Jews' are the ones being answered.

problems.why: Judges 8:31 calls Abimelech son of Gideon by a concubine, but the genealogy is not 'traced' in the sense of being in a formal genealogy like Matthew/Luke; this is a stretch as parallel.
problems.fix: Acknowledge this is narrative, not genealogical list.

problems.quote: But the wretched people do not even know the next line
problems.why: 'Next line' is ambiguous—next line of Scripture or of the opponents' argument?
problems.fix: Clarify: the next words of Scripture, 'being made like the Son of God.'

problems.quote: born of a prostitute and yet had their genealogy traced—immediately Solomon, born of Uriah's wife
problems.why: Bathsheba was not a prostitute; the argument conflates her with other women.
problems.fix: Clarify the tradition or correct the characterization of Bathsheba.

edits.old: But the wretched people do not even know the next line:
edits.new: But the wretched people do not even know the next words of Scripture:

edits.old: To them we will answer: You have spoken wrongly.
edits.new: To the Jews we will answer: You have spoken wrongly.

fixed: Glossary order issue: The source itself varies the order (ἀπάτορα... ἀμήτορα in the interlocutor's question, then ἀπάτορα καὶ ἀμήτορα in the final clause), so the English faithfully mirrors the source's own variation; no edit needed.
Speaker marking: The source introduces the interlocutor with 'ἀλλ' ἴσως τις ἐπερωτᾷ τῶν ἀκροατῶν καὶ λέγει' and the answer with 'Πρὸς ὃν ἐροῦμεν', which the English already renders; no edit needed.
Speaker clarity: The source says 'Πρὸς οὓς ἐροῦμεν' (to whom we will say), referring back to 'Ἰουδαῖοι' (the Jews); the English 'them' is ambiguous, so clarified to 'the Jews'.

Wrong scripture: The source itself cites Solomon and Abimelech as examples of those born of a prostitute and genealogized (γενεαλογηθέντας); the English accurately renders the source's claim, so no edit needed.
Speaker ambiguity: The source says 'τὸν ἐπιόντα στίχον' (the coming verse), referring to the next verse of Scripture; clarified to 'next words of Scripture'.

Mistranslation: The source says 'ἐκ πόρνης γεννηθέντας' (born from a prostitute) and lists Solomon from Uriah's wife as an example; the English accurately renders the source's own conflation, so no edit needed.
